clue.text: Section of roast rib alarmed family

definitions.note: used attributively, as in a family feud

indicators.note: a section is a slice cut from the middle of something, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of roast, all of rib and the start of alarmed

explanation.surface: Carving the Sunday joint upsets the relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes what belongs to a tribe or clan, so it works as an attributive word for kin, as in tribal or family loyalties.

clue.text: One willing in trial on a hill

blocks.note: a test is a trial
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A volunteer for an experiment on a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' reads as eager, but here it means making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, so someone who wills property to heirs.

clue.text: Protection from one small measure with agreement

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
mm, the millimetre, is a small unit of length
unity is harmony or agreement

explanation.surface: Signing a deal brings a little safety.
explanation.definitionFit: Immunity is protection or exemption, from disease or from prosecution.

clue.text: A path out

blocks.note: taken as written
a way is a path or route

explanation.surface: A route that leads outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out is not at home, which is also what being away means.

clue.text: One living through mutated virus getting very yellow

indicators.note: a mutated thing has had its make-up changed, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
V is the standard abbreviation for very
or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A patient coming through an infection turns jaundiced.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic term for gold, used in crosswords for yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A survivor is a person who lives through an ordeal such as a disaster or an illness.

clue.text: Unusually furtive Minoan giving little away

indicators.note: something done unusually departs from the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A secretive ancient Cretan keeps their cards close to the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: Minoans were the Bronze Age civilisation of Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uninformative tells little, so it gives little information away.

clue.text: Church official consuming, for example, revolting but endless dish

indicators.note: to revolt is to turn over, so the abbreviation before it is turned round
without an end means the final letter is cut off
consuming means eating up and taking inside, so the official holds the rest

blocks.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
taken as written, losing its last letter
a verger is a church caretaker and attendant

explanation.surface: A verger eats a disgusting meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like disgusting, describing the dish, but it means turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegeburger is a patty of vegetables shaped like a hamburger, served as a dish.

clue.text: Confirm fuel returned after five and before end of day

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards
'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'day'

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for five
to fire is to fuel or stoke, as in firing a furnace
the final letter of day

explanation.surface: Checking that fuel was given back after five o'clock, before the day ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' is the selection signal for the last letter of day.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify is to check and confirm that something is true.

clue.text: Vegetable and bread regularly found on plate

indicators.note: at regular intervals means taking every second letter

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: A salad of vegetable and bread is always there on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a crisp red root vegetable eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Island in South Africa with giant old bird

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for South Africa
the moa was a huge flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct

explanation.surface: A traveller spots a huge extinct bird on an island off South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island in South Africa' reads as one phrase, but the island is in the Pacific; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is a group of islands in the South Pacific, and the name is used for its main island state.

clue.text: Laughed unpleasantly as drinks knocked back by German editor

indicators.note: knocking back is drinking, but read literally it sends the word backwards

blocks.note: gins are drinks, to be turned round
a standard abbreviation for German
the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A German editor downs several drinks while others snigger at him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' fits the drinking scene so well that it hides its job of turning the drinks round.
explanation.definitionFit: To snigger is to laugh in a half-suppressed, sneering or disrespectful way.

clue.text: Bone cut by knife

blocks.note: shoulder is a cut of meat, as of lamb or pork
a blade is a knife

explanation.surface: A butcher slices through a bone with a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut by knife' reads as a description of the bone; it is two pieces, a butcher's cut followed by a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoulder blade, or scapula, is the flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder.

clue.text: First class single left out

indicators.note: something out has been removed, so the letter for left is taken away

blocks.note: single and alone both mean unaccompanied
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A lone first-class ticket has been left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A1, from the top grade in Lloyd's Register of ships, means excellent or first-rate.

clue.text: Turn over following mistake

blocks.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone flips the page after spotting an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn over' reads as a phrasal verb, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is an informal word for a silly blunder or error.

clue.text: Polishes fans

blocks.note: first meaning: rubs to a shine
second meaning: enthusiasts

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as people waving fans or Poles who are fans; the capital on Polishes hides the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Buff is both a verb for rubbing a surface to a shine and a noun for an expert enthusiast.

clue.text: Put forward one single department to be located

blocks.note: to posit is to put forward an idea
the Roman numeral for one
single and one both mean a solitary unit
D is an abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: Proposing that a lone section should be found somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Something positioned has been placed or set in a particular location.

clue.text: Get more votes than unpopular European we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word's sound, so the spelling of the word before it is swapped for one that sounds the same

blocks.note: out of fashion, out of favour
a Pole is a person from Poland

explanation.surface: An election rival who is a disliked European still tops the ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: To outpoll a rival is to receive a larger number of votes in an election.

clue.text: Bloody exceptional

blocks.note: first meaning: of meat, lightly cooked and still red inside
second meaning: uncommon, unusually good

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' looks like a British intensifier, as in bloody exceptional; it is the steak sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare steak is barely cooked and bloody inside, and rare also means seldom found or remarkable.

clue.text: Proficient testament to benevolence

blocks.note: good at something means proficient in it
a last will and testament

explanation.surface: A well-drafted will that leaves a legacy to charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill is friendly, kindly feeling toward others, the same as benevolence.

clue.text: You and I left guide around start of route being knowledgeable

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the guide word wraps the letter that follows
'start of' keeps only the first letter of 'route'

blocks.note: we is you and I together
L is the standard abbreviation for left
to lead is to guide
the first letter of route

explanation.surface: We set off with a guide who knows the route well.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-read person has read widely, and so is broadly knowledgeable.

clue.text: Sack of iron concealing iridium

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it within, so one symbol goes inside the other

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Ir is the chemical symbol for iridium

explanation.surface: A bag of iron ore secretly holds a rarer metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag of metal but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack and to fire are both informal verbs for dismissing someone from a job.

clue.text: Adult introducing bridge partners gets a little formidable

blocks.note: A is the old film-classification letter for adult
West and East sit opposite each other as partners at the bridge table
some means a small amount

explanation.surface: A grown-up who brings in a pair of card players becomes a little scary.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are named by compass points, and N-S and E-W are the partnerships.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome in its older sense means inspiring awe or dread, much as formidable does.

clue.text: Sketch artist perhaps lifting prize

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something raises it from bottom to top, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: one who draws, an example of a sketch artist, as perhaps signals

explanation.surface: An illustrator walks off with an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward and a prize are both something given in recognition of achievement.

clue.text: Endlessly devoured strange work

indicators.note: without ends means both outer letters are dropped
something strange is out of its usual form, so the remaining letters are reordered

blocks.note: the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone tore through an odd book from cover to cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devoured' fits a reader racing through a book, which hides that it is the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: An oeuvre is a work of art or literature, or an artist's whole body of work.

clue.text: Fragrant resin carried back by regime leaders

indicators.note: something carried is held inside, so the letters lie within the following words
going back means reading from right to left

blocks.note: the letters span the end of regime and the start of leaders

explanation.surface: The heads of a regime ship back an exotic perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant gum resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Temporary setback as male dropped from aircraft

indicators.note: something dropped from a whole is taken out of it, so a letter goes

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
a blimp is a non-rigid airship

explanation.surface: A man falling out of a plane is a setback, to put it mildly.
explanation.definitionFit: A blip is a brief, minor deviation or problem, soon put right.

clue.text: God of wildfowl oddly missing

indicators.note: the odd-numbered positions are lost, leaving only every other letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A duck deity has strangely disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image worshipped as a god, and by extension a god itself.

clue.text: Cut perhaps not popular with panel

indicators.note: not means without, so the word for popular is removed

blocks.note: a cut is an example of an injury, as perhaps signals
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An unpopular budget cut faces a review panel.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury is a panel of people sworn to give a verdict, or to judge a competition.

clue.text: Vegan data possibly showing benefit

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Statistics on plant-based diets might show they are good for you.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage and a benefit are both a favourable gain or circumstance.

clue.text: Wed posh idiot with energy

blocks.note: U means upper-class, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An upper-class fool marries someone lively.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the convention for upper-class or posh.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed is to join in marriage, and to unite is to join together.

clue.text: Exploit involving record day with unknown going through

definitions.note: read as thoroughgoing, with its halves swapped

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the following pieces are placed inside

blocks.note: a deed is a heroic act or exploit
an EP is an extended-play record
D is the abbreviation for day
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A daring feat involving a record and a day, with a mystery element passing through it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a play on thoroughgoing, with going put before through.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-dyed means thoroughgoing or out-and-out, like cloth dyed right through, as in a deep-dyed villain.

clue.text: Look at top batter?

blocks.note: to eye is to look at
a lid is a top or cover

explanation.surface: A selector checks out the opening batsman in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top batter' suggests the leading batsman; the question mark flags that batter means something that bats, as an eyelid does.
explanation.definitionFit: We bat our eyelids, so an eyelid is whimsically a thing that bats.
